title: Patterns Everywhere
about: Train a tiny model on labelled examples and watch it guess.

cards.prompt: Teach the computer (the **model**): tap **Apple** or **Banana** for each fruit.
cards.hint: Read each fruit's name: is it an apple or a banana?
cards.nudge: Check the names again: each one says whether it's an apple or a banana.
cards.explanation: Your labels were right. The computer then guessed from the **nearest** labelled fruit, and called the **yellow apple** a banana. The next card shows why.

cards.title: What just happened
cards.body:
You made **training data**: examples, each with a **label** saying what it is. From them the computer built a **model**: its way of guessing labels for new things.

Every apple it saw was red, so the yellow apple sat nearest the bananas.

cards.prompt: What would help this model most with yellow apples?

options.text: Add some yellow apples to its training data
Add lots more red apples, big and small
options.nudge: It already knows red apples. What kind of apple is it missing?

options.text: Add more bananas, so it knows them better
options.nudge: Would more bananas teach it anything new about apples?

options.text: Remove the bananas from its training data
options.nudge: Then it couldn't spot bananas at all. What could you add instead?

cards.hint: The model only knows what it was shown. What was it never shown?
cards.explanation: It went wrong because it had never seen a **yellow apple**, so adding some teaches it apples can be yellow. More red apples or bananas teach it nothing new about apples.

cards.hint: Which example looks most like the yellow apple?
cards.nudge: Look at the fruit it gets wrong. Which example is most like it?
cards.explanation: The **golden apple** shows apples can be yellow, so the yellow apple now sits nearest an apple. Another red apple or banana doesn't change that.

cards.prompt: Put the steps of teaching a computer in order, first to last.
cards.hint: Think of the fruit: you needed fruit before labelling it, and tested guesses before trusting them.
cards.nudge: Start by gathering examples. What must happen to them before the model can learn?
cards.explanation: **Collect** examples, **label** them and **train** the model. Then **test** it on new examples, like your test fruit, before you **use** it for real.

cards.prompt: It copies its **3 closest** examples. Label the fruit.
cards.hint: The names tell you each label. Lemons are yellow and fairly round.
cards.nudge: Check the names again: each one says apple, banana or lemon.
cards.explanation: Your labels were right. But the **yellow apple**'s 3 nearest examples were all lemons, so it guessed lemon. It had never seen a yellow apple.

cards.prompt: The model knows only apple and banana, and passed every test. Will it name a **green pear** right?

options.text: No: it can only say apple or banana, so it's wrong
Yes: it passed every test, so it can do any fruit
options.nudge: Passing 3 tests shows it's good at apples and bananas. Can it name a pear?

options.text: Yes: it will notice it's new and add a pear label
options.nudge: Where would a new label come from, if nobody taught it one?

options.text: Yes, if the pear sits nearest an apple on the chart
options.nudge: Then it would say apple. Is a pear an apple?

cards.hint: List every answer this model is able to give. Is "pear" one of them?
cards.explanation: It can only pick labels it learned, so it will say **apple** or **banana** and be wrong. Passing tests only shows it's good at what was tested.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Training data** is examples, each with a **label** saying what it is.
- The computer finds patterns and builds a **model** to guess new things.
- It only knows what it was shown, so use varied examples.

Next: what AI can't do.
